R739.note: Extension now derived from the server-side contentTypeToExt map keyed by the already-validated detected type, so the allowlist gate and the storage decision agree; every allowed type has a map entry and legitimate uploads still return the stored name.

R740.note: Canonicalises base and combined path and rejects when GetRelativePath yields a rooted or '..'-prefixed result, which closes traversal; only edge cost is a legitimate filename literally starting with '..' being refused, and the success path is unchanged.

R741.note: Deleting the .csrf(ignoringRequestMatchers) customizer restores Spring Security's default CSRF filter for the billing PATCH; no other exclusion existed in this chain, so nothing else is broadened or narrowed and token-bearing clients still get the queued result.

R742.note: Registers /settings/email on protectedMux so the email change goes through the CSRF-protected chain; profile stays put, the 405 non-POST branch and 202 success are untouched, and the now-unused apiMux parameter is legal Go and keeps the signature stable.

R743.note: Swaps run-report.bat for a run-report.exe that nothing in the case shows exists (the doc comment says the work lives in the batch script), so cmd.exe re-entry is avoided only by invoking a missing binary; the write-up asserts the .exe as fact, so the endpoint silently fails with IOException for every legitimate report name.

R744.note: Removes [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] so the app-wide AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute registered in Program.cs validates the POST again; the action body, validation, and RedirectToAction are byte-identical otherwise.

R745.note: Passing username as Winston metadata does neutralise CRLF/ANSI injection, but the fix also switches the logger's global format from simple() to json(), changing the shape of every log line the app emits; that is mentioned only in passing inside a parsability bullet and was not needed, since simple() JSON-stringifies metadata too.

R746.note: Query structure is now a fixed 'LIKE ?' with the wildcard-wrapped term bound at execute(), preserving the same '%term%' substring semantics while quotes and wildcards in the term can no longer alter the statement.

R747.note: Template source is now an application-controlled literal with name passed as a Jinja context variable, so injected {{...}} is data rather than template code; autoescaping only entity-encodes markup that was never meant to render, leaving legitimate greetings identical.

R748.note: Replaces the variable-variable dispatch with a lookup in a hardcoded map and calls only the mapped handler name, so only clearCache and purgeSessions are reachable; the allowlist matches the two functions the file defines, i.e. the documented contract, so no legitimate command is lost.

R749.note: JWT::decode with a Key bound to HS256 verifies the signature before claims are read and returns null on any failure, keeping the same ['id','role'] return shape; the new JWT_SECRET requirement is inherent to signature verification and is stated in the write-up.

R750.note: exec(String[]) removes the StringTokenizer argument splitting that let host inject extra tokens, and the output/response path is unchanged; residual gap is that a host beginning with '-' is still read as a ping flag, which the write-up does not mention.

R751.note: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') replaces Math.random for the reset token; only observable change is a longer, unpredictable token value, which is the point of the fix, and storage, email, and response are untouched.

R752.note: SecureRandom.nextBytes into a per-request 16-byte buffer, Base64url-encoded, replaces Random.nextFloat for the remember-me key; cookie flags, session attribute, and response text are unchanged. The prose claim that the bytes are 'generated once and reused across requests' misdescribes the code, which correctly draws fresh bytes each request.

R753.note: Encode.forHtml from OWASP Java Encoder is applied to both authorName and comment before concatenation, the correct context for HTML element text; page structure, logging, and content type are unchanged.
